page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.vgn6i-m8-vws.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The configuration includes 10 dedicated vCPUs derived from 5 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is set at 46.0 GB, yielding 4.6 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage options, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

A key differentiator of this instance is the inclusion of a fractional NVIDIA T4 GPU (0.5x allocation) providing 8 GB of dedicated VRAM. The underlying Intel Xeon CPU supports Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX and AVX512F), cryptography acceleration via AES, and bit manipulation instructions (BMI2, ADX, FMA). However, it lacks newer instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI, AVX VNNI, and AMX.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance profile. Single-core CPU performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories, respectively. Multi-core performance is more resilient, achieving average ratings in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth remains average across both small and large block read/write operations, though PassMark memory scores are weak. For specialized tasks, the instance delivers average performance in ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation, but struggles with text processing and single-threaded compression.

Given the fractional GPU allocation and moderate CPU performance, this instance offers a cost-efficient entry point for workloads requiring GPU acceleration without the expense of a full dedicated GPU. It is suitable for light LLM inference on small models (under 1B parameters), where it achieves average token generation speeds, whereas performance drops significantly on larger 7B models. Other appropriate workloads include entry-level 3D rendering, image processing, and general-purpose applications that benefit from hardware-accelerated graphics or parallel computing.
